findings.description: CARRIED, STATUS NOT_FIXED FOR THE THIRD CONSECUTIVE ROUND. Round 5 flagged two false claims; the round-6 fix corrected them and missed a third site; the follow-up corrected that; this round finds the rewritten paragraph asserting DIFFERENT false universals. Three rewrites, wrong in a new way each time. RESOLUTION TAKEN: this project's standing waiver ruling -- when a defect family survives repeated rounds against the same mechanism, remove the mechanism rather than guard it again -- applied to explanatory prose rather than to code. The over-reaching sentences are DELETED rather than rewritten a fourth time; what survives is limited to what this spec itself tests, with the classification decision table left to cmd_classify as the source of truth and to Section 4 of this same file, which tests all six verdicts directly.

findings.evidence: green-check.test.sh:751-759 claims another concurrent run or unrelated process has a different PGID; :808-815 select and kill every ppid-1, same-PGID, exact-argv process. The file supports direct `bash green-check.test.sh` invocation at :85-87 and concedes at :834-836 that plain backgrounding without job control inherits the script PGID. META-2 at :858-889 constructs only a DIFFERENT-PGID bystander, so it cannot detect the same-PGID case. Reparenting changes PPID but not PGID.
findings.description: CARRIED, STATUS PARTIAL. Adding PGID fixes the normal run-tests.sh case, because that runner enables job control and each spec gets its own process group. It does NOT establish ownership for every supported invocation: two concurrent DIRECT invocations launched from one non-job-controlled shell share a PGID, so each can still select and kill the other's reparented sleep. The comment asserting that a concurrent run has a different PGID is true only under job control -- another false universal. FIX: make ownership survive reparenting WITHOUT depending on the invoking shell's job-control state, via a per-run nonce carried in the spawned process's own argv, and add the SAME-PGID foreign-bystander negative control that META-2 structurally cannot provide.

findings.evidence: Lines 1213-1215 state the release manifest is always in-tree and META 4 never has a reason to skip. Line 1216 guards the block with `[ -f "$RELEASE_TABLE" ]` and lines 1250-1252 emit a META4 SKIPPED line. Lines 113-116 of the same file describe the version-bump-to-freeze window in which the table is legitimately absent.
findings.description: The comment asserts an invariant that the adjacent guard exists precisely to handle, and that the same file elsewhere documents as false during a known window. After plugin.json is bumped but before its manifest is frozen, RELEASE_TABLE is absent and META 4 reports SKIPPED, contradicting the stated invariant. FIX: describe META 4 as conditional during the version-bump window and say why that is acceptable, or make table presence an enforced prerequisite and delete the skip path.

findings.evidence: `git check-ref-format 'refs/tags/v1;printf PWNED'` returns status 1 -- the string contains an ASCII space and is not a legal ref. Legal command-bearing refs do exist: `refs/tags/v1;id` and `refs/tags/v$(id)` both return status 0. The same inaccurate assertion also appears in .claude/scripts/tests/verify-release-manifest.test.sh:282-285.
findings.description: The negative control's comment claims the exact value `v1;printf PWNED` is a legal Git tag and therefore demonstrates injection through an ordinary tag value. The injection class and the fix are REAL and the regression genuinely proves safety against a hostile make-variable override -- but the provenance sentence is false, so the proof is narrower than it claims. This is the defect family in miniature: a true finding carrying an unchecked claim about WHY it is true. FIX: use a genuinely legal command-bearing ref in the proof (strictly stronger), or describe the fixture honestly as an arbitrary hostile make-variable override rather than as a legal tag. Both sites must be corrected.

findings.evidence: Lines 26-27 retain the statement that all jobs run on ubuntu-latest and that shellcheck is pre-installed on the runner image. Lines 118-143 now download and checksum-verify pinned ShellCheck v0.11.0 before invoking `make lint`.
findings.description: The workflow header is stale against what the workflow now does. A maintainer following it could remove or overlook the pinning step believing the runner-provided binary defines the tested version -- which would silently change what the advisory lint job measures. FIX: state that CI installs checksum-pinned ShellCheck 0.11.0, and re-check the rest of that header block against the dolt pinning and git-identity provisioning that also landed in this change set.
